nphi.title: Pacific Public Health Surveillance Network (PPHSN) – LabNet, EpiNet, PacNet, PICNet
nphi.actor: Pacific Community (SPC) – Pacific Public Health Surveillance Network (PPHSN)
nphi.with: Health ministries of Pacific Island countries and territories; WHO; US CDC; ESR/PHF Science; Fiji National University; PIHOA; regional reference laboratories
nphi.summary: Regional surveillance network set up in 1996 under SPC and WHO, with a three-tier laboratory network (regional level-2 labs in Fiji, French Polynesia, Guam and New Caledonia; reference labs in Australia, New Zealand and the US), outbreak…

nphi.title: Lab-based influenza surveillance in Pacific Island countries (PPHSN)
nphi.actor: Institut Pasteur de Nouvelle-Calédonie (with Pacific Community)
nphi.with: Pacific Community (SPC); WHO National Influenza Centre at ESR; WHO CC for Influenza Melbourne; US CDC; Cook Islands, Guam, Wallis and Futuna
nphi.summary: US CDC-funded project from 2006 to set up laboratory-based influenza surveillance in Pacific Island countries, with confirmatory PCR at Institut Pasteur de Nouvelle-Calédonie and training at ESR and the Melbourne WHO collaborating centre.

nphi.title: Drinking-water safety planning training and policy support in the Pacific (WHO/SOPAC)
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: WHO South Pacific; SPC-SOPAC; DASS-NC; Cook Islands
nphi.summary: ESR delivered drinking-water safety planning workshops for Pacific countries from 2006 and helped draft Fiji's national drinking water safety plan for rural and island communities under WHO–SOPAC contracts.

nphi.title: WHO National Influenza Centre support to Pacific laboratories
nphi.actor: ESR (Institute of Environmental Science and Research, now PHF Science)
nphi.with: SPC; WHO; Cook Islands, Guam, Niue, Tokelau, Wallis and Futuna, American Samoa
nphi.summary: As WHO National Influenza Centre, ESR provided influenza laboratory training, reference testing and sentinel surveillance support to Pacific island laboratories in 2006, 2009 and 2010.
